entries.description: When you ask about a file you attached in chat, the assistant's answer is no longer replaced by the knowledge base's no-answer message.

entries.title: Tool test panel runs as the owner only
entries.description: Run as in a tool module's test panel now offers the module's owner, with no sample-values entries for workflows. Type the record a bound input reads and run it.

entries.title: Tools on a new public address save in new workspaces
entries.description: In a workspace that allows any public address, adding a tool on an address nobody listed yet saves it and lists the address in your name, instead of refusing it.

entries.title: Chat menus and widget tiles fit their space
entries.description: The skills and agent menus in chat open below the message box when there is no room above it. Figure tiles in a widget share the row at full width, and a small table in a widget shows without an empty toolbar.

entries.title: A team admin sees only their own team's settings
entries.description: The demo workspace's team admin is now Admin of Operations only, so the settings screens show that team's people, apps and access, and nothing from other teams.

entries.title: A tool from a newer app version says it needs the update
entries.description: A tool that exists only in a newer version of an app now tells the team that an admin takes the update first, instead of saying the tool is not added to the team.

entries.title: Assistants can run your tools over MCP
entries.description: An assistant connected to your team's MCP address, such as Claude or Cursor, now gets the real result when it calls a read tool, instead of an Internal server error. The call runs in the team named in the address, never another team's.

entries.title: Every team can hold the same guardrail
entries.description: A guardrail's name only has to be unique within your team. Making a second one with a name your team already uses now says the name is taken, instead of renaming it with a number.

entries.title: Human Tasks no longer repeats a step's plain fields
entries.description: A task now shows a workflow step's proposal only when two sources disagree, one row per field. Other step details are no longer drawn as extra cards.

entries.title: Human Tasks shows what a workflow step proposes
entries.description: A task from a workflow step now lists the values the step carries. When an email and its attachment disagree, the task shows both case numbers.

entries.title: Knowledge bases show correct counts and jobs
entries.description: A source counts its items, not its pieces. The overview lists recent index jobs, documents show whether they are fresh, stale or have no schedule, files show the right split preset, Add source says why a source cannot be added, and a chat on a test thread of a draft agent opens its connectors.

entries.title: Model key errors link to the page that fixes them
entries.description: When a reply stops because an agent's model key was revoked, expired, missing or out of budget, an admin gets a link to Model providers and a member is told to ask an admin. An error the console has no wording for now reads as one plain sentence, with its code under Details.

entries.title: Starting a scheduled workflow by API checks its input
entries.description: Starting a workflow with a Schedule trigger through the runs API now refuses input that does not fit the trigger's schema, with the same message Start scheduled run gives, instead of starting a run that fails later.

entries.title: The header trail fits, and Govern starts shorter
entries.description: Policies now reads Govern / Policies in the header and no crumb is cut at 1440. In Govern, Activity, Access and Evals start folded so the area shows six rows; open one with its arrow and it stays open.

entries.title: A call fails when the app says so inside a successful answer
entries.description: Some apps, such as Slack, answer a failed call with success and put the error inside, and a plugin can now say where that error sits. The call then fails with the app's own error, or asks you to connect again when the error means the sign-in ended.

entries.title: A new chat says which account it uses
entries.description: When an app has several accounts, a new chat's Connectors list shows the account it starts on, the agent's or the team's default, before the first message.

entries.title: A row you remove right after adding it leaves the list
entries.description: A row you add shows first, marked New, and now leaves the list as soon as you remove, revoke or archive it, instead of staying on screen until you page, search or sort.

entries.title: A run waits when a named account's sign-in ends
entries.description: When the team sign-in of an account a step, agent or chat names expires or is revoked, the run waits until an admin signs that account in again and then goes on, and the chat shows a card to sign it in. No call moves to another account.

entries.title: App names read in full in the chat connectors list
entries.description: For someone who cannot set an app up, the reason to ask an admin now sits under the app's name at every screen width, so the name is no longer cut to a letter or two on a desktop.

entries.title: Every team can add the same skill
entries.description: A skill's name only has to be unique within your team, so several teams can add the same skill from an app.

entries.title: Scrollbars match the light or dark theme
entries.description: Scrollbars in the console are now thin and take their colour from the page, so they no longer look wide and dark on Windows.

entries.title: The assistant hears where an account points, not who
entries.description: The line that tells the assistant which account each app uses names the org or server it points at, and leaves out the person who signed in.

entries.title: Updates name the tools your team is missing
entries.description: When an app's update needs a tool your team cannot call, it is refused and names the tools, so you know which app to turn on.

entries.title: Workflows an agent starts from chat use your app accounts
entries.description: When you ask an agent in chat to start a workflow, its app steps now run as you, with the account you signed in with. Before, those steps were refused with a message that no team member had that email.

entries.title: A new website waits for an admin's approval
entries.description: A website source on an address the account has not allowed waits for an admin to approve its host, as any new outside address does. Nothing is fetched until then, and it syncs once approved.

entries.title: A removed app's card counts its tools
entries.description: The Team setup card of an app that is no longer installed now shows the same number of tools as its Tools tab, not zero.

entries.title: A row you add shows right away
entries.description: When you add a host, a webhook, a team, a key or another row to a list, it shows at the top marked New, even when the list is sorted or searched so it would land on another page.

entries.title: A website sync keeps to the site's pace
entries.description: Changed pages are fetched one at a time at the source's rate, or slower when the site's robots.txt asks for a crawl delay.

entries.title: Add a page works on earlier knowledge bases
entries.description: A knowledge base that already had pages from before typed text sources takes new pages again, keeping the pages and versions it had.

entries.title: App answers have a size cap
entries.description: An answer from an app larger than 25 MB is refused as it arrives, so one huge page can no longer fill the gateway's memory.

entries.title: Ask an admin names someone in the team
entries.description: Ask an admin now names a person granted the role in the team itself, never an admin of every team such as the install's first admin, and says to ask the team's admins when nobody in the team holds it.

entries.title: Changes filter on the server; decisions by right
entries.description: The From filter covers every page, a viewer no longer sees Approve and Reject the server refuses, and a knowledge base's Sources tab follows a sync the schedule started.

entries.title: Chat asks to connect an app nobody has signed in to yet
entries.description: When an app each person signs in to is on for the team but nobody has signed in yet, chat now shows the Connect card naming the app instead of an error, and the assistant names the app too.

entries.title: Chat shows who connects an app's team account
entries.description: When an app is on for the team but its team account is not signed in yet, chat shows a card naming the app: people who manage the team's apps get Connect the team account, and everyone else gets the admins to ask.

entries.title: Clearer counts in Add source pickers
entries.description: Add source's site, library and space pickers say how many you picked and how many are listed, spell libraries correctly, and name a pick the current search hides.

entries.title: Connectors not set up for your team say so
entries.description: On Connectors › Mine, an app your team has not set up now reads Not set up for your team yet, with the admins to ask. An admin's Turn on opens the app's own page instead of a page that does not exist.

entries.title: Document text is fenced as data for AI steps
entries.description: Pages and files reach the questions and FAQ steps marked as data, so text in a document cannot give the model instructions.

entries.title: Documentation sites keep their articles when cleaned
entries.description: A website whose layout carries utility classes or wraps its article in a sidebar element no longer has every page cleaned down to nothing.

entries.title: Files names knowledge snapshots
entries.description: Copies a knowledge source keeps of fetched pages show as Knowledge snapshot in Files, and Storage settings can place them.

entries.title: Knowledge bases show only what you can change
entries.description: People who can read a knowledge base no longer see Add source, Add documents, Add page, Attach sources, Sync now or Detach. Off-for-team apps in the chat picker keep their names on narrow screens, and tab rows show when there is more to scroll to.

entries.title: Knowledge searches name their bases
entries.description: A knowledge search names the knowledge bases it reads, or asks for all of the team's on purpose; an agent's model can no longer widen its own search.

entries.title: Long syncs keep their source to themselves
entries.description: A sync or rebuild renews its hold on its source while it runs, so a long one is never overlapped by another sync or ended as stopped.

entries.title: Meaning search finds small knowledge bases
entries.description: Search by meaning keeps scanning until a small knowledge base beside a large one gets its nearest passages, has its own similarity floor, and says when it found no candidate.

entries.title: Moving the local database checks every row
entries.description: make db-move-image counts every table's rows before and after, refuses a dump that holds fewer rows than it counted, and stops the restore at its first error.

entries.title: Search on SQL Server names its skipped lanes
entries.description: On a database without full-text search, a knowledge search says its keyword lane was skipped instead of failing with a database error.

entries.title: Sync right after a rebuild finishes
entries.description: When a rebuild shows as finished, its source is free: a sync asked at that moment starts instead of saying a run is still going.

entries.title: Turning an app on saves and stops
entries.description: Turning an app on for your team, or saving its settings, now only saves, and the window says members connect their own account from Connectors › Mine. Connecting an account yourself is an optional button after it.

entries.title: Upgrading keeps a base's keyword-only choice
entries.description: The upgrade to meaning search moves only knowledge bases still on the old defaults to both kinds of search, copies every account's pieces on SQL Server too, and a downgrade puts moved bases back.

entries.title: Website and app sources sync on a real stack
entries.description: A source read through an app no longer fails every call on the run's environment, and a setting saved while a rebuild runs is rebuilt as soon as it ends.

entries.title: A file's reading stays in its team
entries.description: When two teams upload the same document, each team's reading of it is its own. One team can no longer see what was read from another team's file.

entries.title: A prep brief shows each count once
entries.description: A section of a meeting prep brief shows how many records it holds in its badge only, not again in its title.

entries.title: A resumed chat still acts as the person who asked
entries.description: A chat reply picked up again after a restart, or after someone approved its change, reads and writes your apps as you, never as the team account; when the chat's person is not known the call is not made.

entries.title: After Connect, the chat carries on
entries.description: When an app needs your sign-in, the reply says it carries on with your ask once you connect, instead of asking you to ask again.

entries.title: An agent reads only the file it names
entries.description: When an agent reads a file by its id, an id written to reach some other part of Files is treated as no file at all, so text inside a document cannot steer an agent into a different request.

entries.title: Answers are not swapped for 'nothing found'
entries.description: When a reply needs a citation, the assistant now only adds the source numbers instead of replacing a correct answer with 'nothing found'. It also states facts about your organisation only from your documents or systems.

entries.title: Asking to think harder in a message uses the deeper model
entries.description: A message that asks the assistant to think harder alongside a question is answered on the deeper model; the Think harder quick reply on its own still answers the last reply again.

entries.title: Attached files cannot pose as instructions
entries.description: Text in an attached file or a knowledge page that tries to end the file's section or add a fake knowledge passage is now shown to the agent as plain text, so a document cannot pass itself off as guidance.

entries.title: Calls that never ran no longer show as errors
entries.description: When a reply reaches its limit, the calls it skipped are no longer listed under the answer as failed steps; the call log still records them.

entries.title: Cards replace the raw tables they came from
entries.description: When the assistant shows a brief or a saved card, the table of the records it read no longer shows above it, and a saved card lists only what changed.

entries.title: Chat connectors show icons and stay open
entries.description: The Connectors button shows the icons of the apps a chat uses, the list shows each app's icon, and checking or unchecking one keeps the list open instead of closing it and opening another page.

entries.title: One record reads as a card, not a one-row table
entries.description: When the assistant reads back a single record, chat shows its fields as a card; the table is still one click away, and two or more records still show as a table.

entries.title: Replies keep their formatting when no source matched
entries.description: A reply that found no matching knowledge passage keeps its lists and paragraphs, with a short note under it, instead of running together as one paragraph.

entries.title: Replies read in order: plan, cards, answer
entries.description: A reply now shows its plan first, its lookups folded into one quiet line you can open, then its cards and the answer; skill loads no longer show in the reply.

entries.title: Reworded replies no longer show a guardrail audit
entries.description: A reply the assistant only reworded at the end no longer shows what a guardrail took back; that note now appears only when a guardrail refused or replaced the answer.

entries.title: Settings lights the page you are on, not its parent
entries.description: On a settings page under Team, such as Webhooks, the sidebar no longer lights Team's General page while your access loads.

entries.title: Short results in chat read cleanly
entries.description: A single record the assistant reads shows as its fields, and a table that fits on one page no longer shows a paging bar.

entries.title: Signing in again as the same user keeps one account
entries.description: Signing in to an app as a user you already linked there updates that account instead of adding a second one, and the window says you are already connected as that user.

entries.title: Turn-on and fix links open the app
entries.description: The Turn on button in chat and on the connectors page, Open on a revoked knowledge source, and Fix the connection on a mailbox deployment now open the app's page instead of a page that does not exist.

entries.title: A file's page no longer reports an outage it does not have
entries.description: A file not yet read for text, or whose stored content is missing, opens without the "can't reach its services" banner. Its preview says what is wrong in its own place.

entries.title: A link to someone else's chat says so
entries.description: Opening a teammate's conversation now says it is someone else's instead of showing a broken page. Pickers, status dots and usage bars carry names a screen reader can read.

entries.title: A refused mailbox is not read again until it changes
entries.description: When a mailbox's password secret or host is refused, the listener stops reading it after the first refusal and says why once, instead of asking again every few seconds. Changing the mailbox on Channels > Email makes it read again.

entries.title: Answers from what was read at the tool limit
entries.description: A reply that runs out of tool calls now answers from the records it already read, instead of saying only that it reached the limit.

entries.title: App updates reach the assistant's skills
entries.description: When an app's new release changes a skill, the update is offered, and turning the app on again gives the assistant the new skill, unless your team edited its copy.

entries.title: Assistant replies name records, not ids
entries.description: The assistant no longer reads the same record twice in one reply, and its replies name records by their title instead of showing internal ids or tool names.

entries.title: Chat tables stay readable on a phone
entries.description: Long values in a chat table are trimmed to the column with the full value on hover, so the first column no longer runs over the next one on a small screen.

entries.title: Follow-ups keep the skill and what was read
entries.description: A follow-up in the same chat keeps the skill the assistant loaded and the records it read, so it answers sooner instead of reading them again.

entries.title: Human Tasks shows only your team's publish reviews
entries.description: A publish review now appears and counts only in the team that owns what it publishes, and a tool's security review only in the Security team. Other teams no longer see or count it, and the team that asked can still open it.

entries.title: Meeting cards read cleanly
entries.description: A prep brief keeps record names on one line beside long details, case numbers stay readable, and a save shows only its saved card.

entries.title: Meetings and record changes are not offered as memories
entries.description: A meeting you mention or a change to a record is no longer offered as something to remember. The assistant offers to remember only lasting preferences, ways of working and facts about you.

entries.title: Plainer replies, workflow pages and failed calls
entries.description: Agents no longer point to results above or below, and a failed tool call says why in words. A workflow page shows its version without a digest, and someone who cannot edit it sees that it is live and who changes it.

entries.title: Row checkboxes appear only when you can act on rows
entries.description: A list shows checkboxes on its rows only when there is something you may do with the rows you pick, so a viewer no longer sees checkboxes that lead nowhere.

entries.title: The assistant can ask which record you mean
entries.description: When logging a meeting, the assistant asks whether to update the client's open opportunity or open a new one, with both as quick replies.

entries.title: The assistant no longer offers to remember one-off asks
entries.description: An instruction for one reply, a request, a question or an app's connection state is not offered as something to remember, so you only see Remember lines for things about you and how you work.

entries.title: The assistant says what it could not read
entries.description: When a lookup fails, the assistant says what could not be read instead of asking whether to try again.

entries.title: Tool calls are read only with the activity permission
entries.description: The tool-call log names who called each tool, so it is now read only by people whose roles hold Activity: view, which reviewers, builders and admins do and viewers do not. A tool's and an app's call history follow the same rule.

entries.title: Uninstalled apps and chat tables read clearly
entries.description: An app the system no longer has installed says your operator installs apps and offers nothing to sign in to. Chat result tables name their columns in words, show dates as dates, leave out empty columns and wrap long text.

entries.title: Viewers no longer add document types
entries.description: Adding a document type, or one from a template, now needs permission to create document types, which viewers do not have. Viewers still keep the team's types up to date and run Extract.

entries.title: Webhooks, usage and storage for who can open them
entries.description: Webhooks and Usage and cost are team-admin pages with their own permissions, and the settings list offers them, and Storage, only to people whose roles open them; anyone else is told so at once, with no failed request behind it.

entries.title: A failed customer lookup reads Failed
entries.description: A customer summary whose customer lookup fails now ends Failed with the error, instead of a successful run that reads Not found. A customer the bank does not have reads Customer not found.

entries.title: A knowledge base shows when it last synced
entries.description: A knowledge base now shows when its sources were last read, the same time its sources show, with when its content last changed underneath. The overview no longer links to a Retrieval tab that does not exist, and people who cannot change the base see no build or refresh buttons.

entries.title: Activity names the workflow behind a tool call
entries.description: A tool call a workflow made shows the workflow's name as its source, not its short id.

entries.title: Agents reach their app tools after a restart
entries.description: An agent's tool calls, such as a Salesforce query, no longer fail with "caller identity is not registered" after the platform's policy service restarts without its settings.

entries.title: Agents show each result once and ask plainly to connect
entries.description: A result already shown as a table is no longer shown again, so answers come back sooner. When you need to connect your own account, the agent asks you to press the Connect button instead of repeating an error code, a link or your email.

entries.title: Audit log and Background only for who can open them
entries.description: The page switcher and search no longer list Audit log and Background to someone their roles keep out, as the sidebar already did, and opening either page without the rights shows why at once instead of asking for data first.

entries.title: Clearer chat tables and sign-in cards
entries.description: A chat table is titled by what it lists, such as Accounts, and leaves out a system's own record details. When a tool needs your account, the card says whether it reads or changes something as you, and the tool shows Needs your sign-in instead of Error.

entries.title: Clearer ids, icons and lists
entries.description: Long ids in tables are shortened at word breaks instead of mid-word, and library widgets read Built in under Updated. The Runs and Audit log pages have their own icons, and lists on Overview, cases and channels read correctly to screen readers.

entries.title: Human Tasks names who asked and keeps the sidebar
entries.description: A tool publish request names the person who asked, not the service that filed it, and a request with no changes says so in words. Reassign shows only to people who may decide the task, and Human Tasks keeps the sidebar like every other page.

entries.title: Lists lead with the record, not its id
entries.description: Every list shows what each row is first and its id last, the same way for every role.

entries.title: One slow service no longer covers a working page
entries.description: The Agents list loads the model list only when you open New agent, and a model list that cannot be read is said in that dialog instead of a banner over the page.

entries.title: Only the Security team is offered Add allowed host
entries.description: A tool on a host that is not allowed shows Add allowed host only to people who manage egress in the Security team. Everyone else reads that saving asks a Security admin in Human Tasks, which is what then happens.

entries.title: Page tabs and wide tables work by keyboard
entries.description: Tabs on Evals and on agent, skill, guardrail, tool, knowledge base and source pages now point a screen reader at the content they show. A table wider than the screen can be focused and scrolled with the arrow keys.

entries.title: Query results show as tables in chat
entries.description: A query's records, such as Salesforce cases, now show in chat as a table instead of a Details card listing the query's totals. Agents also stop re-showing a tool's result, so answers come back sooner.

entries.title: Secrets and your own accounts say what they hold
entries.description: An auth config's client secret is listed by its config's name, and its Used by names that config instead of reading as unused. Your own accounts list tells a connected account whose sign-in has not been named yet apart from one never connected.

entries.title: The Agents list fits its page
entries.description: Long agent descriptions are trimmed to one line, so every agent's id shows with its Copy button.

entries.title: Tool calls name the agent and the workflow
entries.description: The Tool calls page shows the agent and the workflow behind each call by name, each in its own column, instead of an agent id under Workflow.

entries.title: Tools you run act as you
entries.description: On an app where each person signs in, a tool you start in chat or a run you start now uses your own account, and asks you to connect once if you have none, instead of quietly using the team account. The team account serves only runs nobody started, such as schedules and mailboxes.

entries.title: Viewers no longer see buttons they cannot use
entries.description: On Channels a viewer no longer sees Connect channel, Connect, Manage or Embed on a page, and a mailbox's settings open read only with a View only note. An agent page no longer offers a viewer the Test panel, Chat no longer suggests starting a workflow to someone who cannot start one, and a model inventory entry hides its tier, condition and validation actions from whoever cannot change the agent or workflow it describes.

entries.title: Your avatar shows your initials
entries.description: The sidebar avatar shows each person's own initials instead of the same two letters for everyone. Apps and accounts take their initials the same way.

entries.title: A closed sign-in window says so
entries.description: Closing the app's sign-in window before allowing access no longer leaves Connect waiting: it says the window was closed and offers Try again.

entries.title: A missing field is shown
entries.description: When a custom app's Run test needs a field under More settings, such as its test address, that section opens and the field shows why.

entries.title: A refusal names who can act in your workspace
entries.description: When a role's permissions have been edited, a refused action now names the roles that hold it in your workspace, not the roles that hold it by default.

entries.title: A second account signs in where the first does
entries.description: Add account on an app now signs in at the address the app's first account uses, such as your company's Salesforce or GitHub Enterprise address, instead of the public one.

entries.title: Add accounts in any order
entries.description: Add account works on an app with no account yet: the first one you add becomes its default and turns the app on.

entries.title: Connect again asks where to sign in
entries.description: Connecting an app again on Ops AI's own app, such as Salesforce after it was turned on without signing in, now asks where to sign in, starting from where the account signs in now.

entries.title: Connecting an account turns its app on
entries.description: Signing in an account of an app turns the app on for your team, so its tools work and the app reads Connected; there is no separate switch to find.

entries.title: Each workspace's own Security team decides
entries.description: Security reviews, held hosts, workspace secrets and storage settings now follow the Security team named on Settings > Workspace, even when it is not the default team. A workspace that names none has no Security team until an admin names one.

entries.title: Model calls use their own account's provider keys
entries.description: An agent's chat turn now names its account when it reaches the model gateway, so it signs in with that account's saved provider key rather than one account the install named.

entries.title: One state per account
entries.description: An app's Settings show its account's one state, the same as its Auth configs row and its card, with the last test as a line under it.

entries.title: Only what you may do
entries.description: Apps no longer offers Add custom app, the auth configs list or Add selected to someone who may not use them; it says who to ask, and the Connected view says when nothing is connected yet.

entries.title: Ops AI's app asks where each account signs in
entries.description: An auth config that leaves where to sign in unset, such as Ops AI's own app, now asks it in Connect and Add account for each account. An auth config that sets it still decides it for every account on it.

entries.title: Sign in again is asked only after a change
entries.description: The note that accounts must sign in again now shows only once you change where the auth config signs in, its client ID or its permissions. The Connect window waits for the auth config before showing where it signs in.

entries.title: Signed in as a person, not a link
entries.description: An app reads as signed in as the person's username or email, such as their Salesforce username or GitHub login, never the system's identity link or an id.

entries.title: Test an MCP server by listing its tools
entries.description: Test on an MCP server's app now asks the server to list its tools with the account's sign-in, the same call its tools make, so it no longer needs a test address. A server that refuses says why.

entries.title: Your own accounts keep apps after a disconnect
entries.description: The list of apps you can sign in to with your own account now carries each one's state (connected, expired or not connected) and the auth config it signs in through, so an app stays listed after you disconnect it. New auth configs are named after your team, and Ops AI's built-in one reads Ops AI's app.

entries.title: A file cited in chat opens in Files
entries.description: Clicking a file you attached in chat, from the message, its source chip or a citation, opens the file in Files with its preview. A missing record now says so in one plain sentence.

entries.title: Background shows the knowledge schedule
entries.description: Govern › Background lists the knowledge schedule with its state on installs that have plugins.

entries.title: Connect finishes in any window
entries.description: A sign-in finishes wherever the app sends you back, even in a new tab or another browser, and the window you started from shows Connected. A refusal shows one plain sentence naming who acts.

entries.title: Email texts in Files are named and filtered
entries.description: The text of a received email is stored under its subject, or the sender when there is none, instead of the same name for every email. Files lists email texts only when you filter for them, and a run or case that used one still opens it.

entries.title: Files you attach in chat are read and kept in Files
entries.description: A file attached to a chat message is stored in Files as a chat attachment, the agent reads it to answer, and the message links to it. A file the agent cannot read, such as a scan with no text, is named in the reply with the reason.

entries.title: Test runs never change a live account unasked
entries.description: A write tried in a test run on an app's live account now waits for someone's approval, even when the person testing could approve writes themselves. Add a test account to the app to try writes freely.

entries.title: Uploads are typed the same on every server
entries.description: An executable renamed to a PDF is now recognised as an executable on Linux servers as well as on Macs.

entries.title: A file read as full text says so
entries.description: After Full text, a file's header reads "Read as full text" instead of "Not read", and still does after the page reloads.

entries.title: Every plugin tool reaches its own system
entries.description: A plugin's request-template tools and MCP tools now reach the plugin's own addresses without Security listing them, as its code tools already did; a call to any other address still needs the allowed list.

entries.title: Running an app's tool from its page
entries.description: Real on a tool page runs in Production when the app is set up only for Production, instead of asking for Test. An app tool's answer shows shaped once, with no false transform error, and the Request sent tab shows the request that went out.

entries.title: Salesforce tools reach your org
entries.description: Salesforce tools read cases again, whether they run on the team account or on a person's own sign-in. On an app where everyone signs in with their own account, a person can use its tools before anyone signs in the team account.

entries.title: An app shows Connected only once it works
entries.description: Turning an app on or saving its keys no longer marks it Connected. An app reads Connected after the team account signs in or Test connection passes, and shows when its sign-in has expired or was refused.

entries.title: An app's tool page names your team's account
entries.description: A tool from an app your team connected shows the team's account it runs with, instead of saying it has no connection yet.

entries.title: Approvals show fields inside records, row by row
entries.description: When a call changes a record that holds other records, an approver now sees each inner field as its own row, in chat and on the run page, instead of one flattened line.

entries.title: Asking for two approvers turns a tool's approval on
entries.description: Choosing two approvers for a tool now also turns its approval on, so its writes wait for both people.

entries.title: Forms are members-only until public pages are on
entries.description: A workflow shared as a form is offered to signed-in team members only; the link anyone can open appears once your install turns public form pages on.

entries.title: Roles, sign-ins and limits hold as given
entries.description: A person holds only the roles they were given, removing someone from a team removes their saved sign-ins to other systems, and limits apply to each key, person and address. One busy key or a guessing address no longer spends everyone's allowance.

entries.title: Sample team installs when a document type is shared
entries.description: When another team already holds a document type the sample team needs, it now gets its own copy under the team's prefix, and the workflows that read that type follow it. Reading a file with a seeded workflow is covered by a test.

entries.title: Tool call history shows only your team's calls
entries.description: Tool call history and an app's usage list only the calls your team made, also on apps every team shares, and each call says whether it ran as a person's own account or the team account.

entries.title: A knowledge source of any type opens its page
entries.description: A knowledge source read through a plugin, such as Salesforce articles, now opens its page, shows as a Plugin source and syncs from there. A source of a type the console does not know yet opens under its own name instead of a blank error page.

entries.title: A tool fills its query placeholders
entries.description: A tool operation whose address held a placeholder in the query, such as ?email={email}, sent the placeholder itself instead of the value. It now sends the value, and leaves the parameter out when no value is given.

entries.title: Adding a knowledge source works again
entries.description: Add source on a knowledge base was refused with a validation error for every kind of source, so no files could be added from the console. Adding a source to a knowledge base works again for every source type.

entries.title: Embedded chat widgets start sessions again
entries.description: A bank's server could not mint a widget session with its deployment's key, and the widget page could not load its settings, because the deployment was not found. Both work again, and each still reads only the one deployment its key or session names.

entries.title: A failed tool call no longer stalls a workflow
entries.description: When a tool call fails before the connected system answers, the step now ends as failed instead of waiting forever. Saving an operation whose body puts a placeholder inside quotes is refused with the placeholder named, since that body could never be sent.

entries.title: Every workflow run ends with a clear outcome
entries.description: A run nobody is working on shows as Stuck with its reason, and Retry resumes it without sending anything twice. A timed-out change, a short tools outage, a long Human Tasks list or an email that will not start no longer leaves a run silently broken.

entries.title: Every flow is checked each night, in your devcontainer too
entries.description: The nightly checks now run each use case on its own fresh database and get past the first step again, so a page that broke during the day is named the next morning. Use cases also run inside the Ops AI devcontainer, against its own database and policy service.

entries.title: Approvals go to your own team
entries.description: A step waiting for approval now goes to approvers in the run's own team.

entries.title: Docs pages keep working while they are edited
entries.description: A documentation page being changed no longer breaks the docs site; the other pages stay open while it is edited.

entries.title: Pages open for your own team after sign-in
entries.description: A link opened straight after sign-in now loads for a team you belong to. A record in another team says so and offers to switch.
